prompt: Implement histogram to count how many times each score 0-9 appears, returning an int array of length 10 where index i holds the count of score i.
explanation: A counting array turns the value being counted into an index: counts[score]++ files each score into its own bucket in a single pass. Because new int arrays start out filled with zeros, no separate initialization loop is needed. This counting pattern is the basis of counting sort and frequency tables.
hints: Allocate int[] counts = new int[10]; Java fills it with zeros automatically.
The score itself is the index: for each score s, do counts[s]++.
An enhanced for loop (for (int s : scores)) is enough -- you never need the position in the input.
